method: Piecewise fitted kinematics with explicitly assumed cruise and high-speed continuation.
assumptions: Course timing starts at launch; no initial idle is added.
Course 2 inserts constant-speed cruising to complete 600 ft.
Course 3 assumes rest-to-rest motion; cruise speed is solved for 1320 ft in 60 s.
Cruise RPM uses the acceleration-phase speed curve.
Cruise fuel is the midpoint of acceleration/deceleration rate curves; endpoints are scenario bounds, not confidence bounds.
Course 4 continues positive acceleration exponentially after the common calibration interval or 80% of the zero-acceleration time.
Beyond measured speed, RPM uses a held effective ratio and fuel holds its boundary rate.
Phase changes can create acceleration, RPM and fuel-rate steps; distance and speed remain continuous.
Camry fuel economy is mi/lb; unknown fuel density prevents reporting MPG.
Zero fitted fuel rate makes instantaneous fuel economy undefined, shown as a gap.

continuation.sensitivity_description: Decay time constant multiplied by 0.5 and 2; assumption sensitivity, not a confidence interval.
